item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 251154
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM PDT Tue Aug 25 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Lala, located several hundred miles north of Pearl and Hermes
Atoll, on Tropical Storm Iselle, located several hundred miles
west of the southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula, and on
recently upgraded Tropical Storm Julio, located well southwest of
the southern tip of Baja California Peninsula.

The National Hurricane Center has issued the last advisory on the
remnants of Tropical Depression Moke, located several hundred miles
east of Johnston Island,

Central East Pacific:
A tropical wave located well to the south of southern Mexico is
producing a large area of disorganized showers and thunderstorms.
Environmental conditions appear favorable for development of this
system, and a tropical depression is expected to form in a few days
while it moves generally west-northwestward at 10 to 15 mph, well
offshore of Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...30 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

Western East Pacific:
A trough of low pressure located well to the east-southeast of the
Hawaiian Islands is producing some disorganized showers and
thunderstorms. An area of low pressure is forecast to form along the
trough during the next couple of days, and environmental conditions
appear conducive for some gradual development thereafter. A tropical
depression could form during the latter part of the week or early
this weekend while the system drifts generally north-northeastward.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...30 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...60 percent.

Well Offshore of Southern Mexico:
An area of low pressure could form well offshore of Central America
late this week or this weekend. Environmental conditions could
support some gradual development of this system, and a tropical
depression could form late this weekend or early next week while it
moves westward to west-northwestward at 10 to 15 mph well offshore
of southern Mexico.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...40 percent.

&&
Public Advisories on Tropical Storm Julio are issued under
WMO header WTPZ35 NHC and under AWIPS header MIATCPEP5.
Forecast/Advisories on Tropical Storm Julio are issued under
WMO header WTPZ25 and under AWIPS header MIATCMEP5.

$$
Forecaster Blake

item.title: Tropical Storm Iselle Public Advisory Number 9
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM PDT Tue Aug 25 2026 
000
WTPZ34 KNHC 251442
TCPEP4
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Iselle Advisory Number   9
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP092026
800 AM PDT Tue Aug 25 2026
 
...LARGE ISELLE FORECAST TO SLOWLY WEAKEN DURING THE NEXT FEW 
DAYS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 AM PDT...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...20.9N 121.1W
ABOUT 730 MI...1175 KM W OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...70 MPH...110 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...WNW OR 295 DEGREES AT 10 MPH...17 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...988 MB...29.18 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 AM PDT (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Iselle was
located near latitude 20.9 North, longitude 121.1 West. Iselle is
moving toward the west-northwest near 10 mph (17 km/h), and this 
general motion is expected for the next couple of days, with a turn 
towards the west possible on Thursday.
 
Maximum sustained winds remain near 70 mph (110 km/h) with higher
gusts.  Slow weakening is forecast during the next few days.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 205 miles (335 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 988 mb (29.18 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Iselle are affecting the west coast of the
Baja California Peninsula, and will continue for a couple more days.
These swells are likely to cause life-threatening surf and rip
current conditions. Please consult products from your local weather
office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 PM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Blake

item.title: Tropical Storm Iselle Forecast Discussion Number 9
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM PDT Tue Aug 25 2026 
000
WTPZ44 KNHC 251444
TCDEP4
 
Tropical Storm Iselle Discussion Number   9
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP092026
800 AM PDT Tue Aug 25 2026

Iselle continues to produce a large area of deep convection near 
and well northeast of the center.  A GCOM-AMSR2 microwave 
pass from a few hours ago showed that the system is on the edge of 
the convective mass, and the low-level center is displaced to the 
southwest of the mid-level circulation.  Satellite estimates support 
keeping Iselle a 60-kt tropical storm for this advisory.  Gradual 
weakening is anticipated during the next few days due to persistent 
westerly shear, cooling waters and a dry mid-level atmosphere. 
Iselle should lose all deep convection in about 2 days due to a
hostile environment, and post-tropical status is anticipated after 
that time.  Model guidance is in very good agreement on the slow 
decay, and no significant changes were made to the last NHC 
forecast.

Microwave fixes indicate that Iselle has turned, and is now moving 
west-northwestward at about 9 kt.  This general heading should 
continue for the next couple of days due to ridging extending from 
the southern United States.  As the storm weakens, it should turn 
more westward by day 3 due to the cyclone becoming steered more by 
the low-level flow.  There has been a modest leftward shift in the 
guidance, consistent with a weakening system, so the new forecast is 
shifted to the left, lying between the NOAA corrected-consensus 
model HCCA and the Google DeepMind ensemble mean.

NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP102026

...JULIO A LITTLE STRONGER BUT SHOULD BECOME ABSORBED BY ISELLE 
LATER TODAY...

----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...18.0N 118.9W
ABOUT 675 MI...1085 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA

PRESENT MOVEMENT...NNE OR 15 DEGREES AT 22 MPH...35 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1001 MB...29.56 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 AM PDT (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Julio was
located near latitude 18.0 North, longitude 118.9 West. Julio is
moving toward the north-northeast near 22 mph (35 km/h).  This 
general motion is expected to continue today. 
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 50 mph (85 km/h) with higher gusts.
Little change in strength is forecast before Julio becomes absorbed 
by Tropical Storm Iselle later today.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 175 miles (280 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1001 mb (29.56 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.

item.title: Tropical Storm Julio Forecast Discussion Number 4
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM PDT Tue Aug 25 2026 
534 
WTPZ45 KNHC 251446
TCDEP5
 
Tropical Storm Julio Discussion Number   4
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP102026
800 AM PDT Tue Aug 25 2026

Satellite images show that the center of Julio is becoming exposed 
on the northern side of an area of strong convection.  Most of the 
intensity estimates are higher than before, so the initial wind 
speed is nudged upward to 45 kt, which is also consistent with a 
recent OSCAT scatterometer pass.  Julio shouldn't last long since 
shear is greatly increasing as the cyclone gets closer to the 
much-larger Tropical Storm Iselle.  It is forecast by all of the 
models to break apart later today as Julio becomes a small trough a 
low pressure rotating around Iselle's eastward side.  Little change 
in strength is forecast before Julio dissipates tonight, and it 
wouldn't be surprising if scatterometer data showed Julio 
dissipated by the afternoon.  The 12-h forecast below is mostly 
given as a placeholder to show the wind field as separate from 
Iselle until they combine tonight.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
 
INIT  25/1500Z 18.0N 118.9W   45 KT  50 MPH
 12H  26/0000Z 20.8N 119.0W   45 KT  50 MPH
 24H  26/1200Z...DISSIPATED
